What is CIBIL score?: A CIBIL score is a 3-digit numeric summary of your credit history, rating your creditworthiness on a scale of 300 to 900.
What is a good CIBIL score?: A CIBIL score of 750 or above is considered excellent and increases your chances of getting quick loan approvals at lower rates.
What is collateral?: Collateral is an asset or property pledged by a borrower to secure a loan. The bank can seize it if the loan defaults.
What is a co applicant?: A co-applicant is a co-borrower who signs the loan agreement along with the primary borrower, sharing the repayment liability.
What is loan tenure?: Loan tenure is the duration or time period agreed upon by the bank and the borrower for the repayment of the loan.
What is foreclosure?: Foreclosure is paying off the entire remaining loan amount before the scheduled maturity date, closing the account early.
What is prepayment?: Prepayment is paying a part of your outstanding loan amount before the scheduled EMI date to reduce your tenure or EMI.
What are prepayment charges?: Prepayment charges are fees levied by banks when you pay off your loan early (usually zero for floating rate home loans).
What is a guarantor?: A guarantor is a person who promises to repay the borrower's loan if the borrower fails to make payments.
What is LTV?: LTV stands for Loan to Value ratio, representing the percentage of the property or vehicle value that the bank can finance.
What is FOIR?: FOIR stands for Fixed Income to Debt Ratio, which lenders use to estimate your monthly repayment capacity based on income.
What happens if I miss an EMI?: Missing an EMI leads to late payment fees, bounce charges, a drop in your CIBIL score, and default notices from the bank.
What is a default?: A default occurs when a borrower fails to repay the loan installments as agreed in the loan contract for over 90 days.
What is CIBIL report?: A CIBIL report is a detailed history of your active and closed loans, payment track records, credit inquiries, and defaults.
Can I get a loan with a low CIBIL score?: You can, but you may face higher interest rates, require a co-applicant, or need to pledge collateral.
What is principal amount?: The principal amount is the actual sum of money borrowed from the bank, excluding any interest or fees.
What is interest amount?: The interest amount is the cost charged by the lender for borrowing the principal sum, calculated based on the interest rate.
What is processing fee?: A processing fee is a one-time administrative charge levied by banks to process and evaluate your loan application.
What is credit history?: Credit history is a record of how you have managed your debt repayments in the past, including credit cards and loans.
What is a soft credit check?: A soft check is a credit file check (like viewing your own score) that does not impact your credit rating.
What is a hard credit check?: A hard credit check is performed by a lender when evaluating a loan application. Too many hard checks can lower your score.
What is a debt consolidation loan?: A personal loan taken to pay off multiple smaller high-interest debts, consolidating them into a single monthly EMI.
What is a top up loan benefit?: A top-up loan provides additional cash on top of an active home loan, offering lower rates than a fresh personal loan.
How can I improve my CIBIL score?: You can improve it by paying EMIs on time, keeping credit card utilization low, and avoiding multiple loan applications.
What is amortization?: Amortization is the process of spreading out loan payments into a series of periodic installments over the agreed tenure.
